misconceptions.description: Treating a bare statement that learning occurred as portfolio evidence, with nothing inspectable attached
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits a reflection asserting growth but no artifact, decision, or trace
misconceptions.feedback: Attach the inspectable thing: an artifact, a documented decision, or a before/after trace. A claim of learning is reflection, not evidence.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a large number of uploaded artifacts demonstrates competency on its own
misconceptions.trigger: learner uploads many unlabeled files expecting volume to stand in for evidence
misconceptions.feedback: Tie each artifact to the specific claim or competency it supports so a reviewer sees what it demonstrates, rather than inferring it from a pile.

misconceptions.description: Submitting AI-authored reflection as evidence of one's own reasoning in a competency portfolio
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits AI-written portfolio text unchanged as personal evidence
misconceptions.feedback: A portfolio certifies your reasoning. Use AI to prompt or organize, but the submitted judgment must be yours and attributable to you.

misconceptions.description: Believing a single best final artifact demonstrates growth in decision-making
misconceptions.trigger: learner includes only a polished final product to show improvement
misconceptions.feedback: Show the trajectory: pair an early and a later artifact and annotate what changed in your reasoning and what evidence drove it.
